NINE BAPTISMS, AND TWO OF THEM WERE NOT IN THIS ARCHIVE

1847 John August · 1848 Henry Jaonas/Hennery James · 1850 George Augustus · 1852 MARGRITH LOUISA MARIA · 1853 William Fredrik · 1855 Catherine Mary Sophia · 1859 Catharina Mary Sophia · 1861 WILLIAM FREDERICK THOMAS · 1863 Frederik Fortunatus. OPEN QUESTION 13 HAS BEEN ASKING WHICH TWO SINCE THIS SITE WAS WRITTEN, and its own note said the index route was closed. IT WAS CLOSED TO A NAME SEARCH AND WAS NEVER CLOSED TO A RELATIONSHIP SEARCH.
yes
MARGRITH LOUISA MARIA, baptised Burgersdorp 5 April 1852
THE INDEX GIVES HER NO SURNAME — EITHER TIME

Two separate index passes of the same page read “Margrith Louisa Maria” and “Margreth Louisa Mary”, and the Name column stops there. IT IS THE BLANK NAME COLUMN AGAIN, the failure that hid her sister Catherine Mary Sophia of 1855 for weeks. Parents entered as “Margrith Willemina Kolbe + John Barry”. ark:/61903/1:1:6VYG-SS94 and 1:1:6F4L-76PK; the image 3:1:3Q9M-CSFQ-QLQN is ON FILM 008039088, the register this archive has been sweeping by hand.

WILLIAM FREDERICK THOMAS BARRY, born 29 September 1861, baptised Graaff-Reinet
INVISIBLE FOR THE OPPOSITE REASON — HE HAS HIS BROTHER'S NAME

William Fredrik Barry was born 23 August 1853 and baptised at Burgersdorp. THIS IS A SECOND WILLIAM FREDERICK, EIGHT YEARS LATER, TO THE SAME PARENTS. A search for William Barry returns the 1853 child and stops, and nothing in the result says there is another. BY THIS FAMILY'S OWN PRACTICE THE FIRST MUST HAVE DIED — a baptism is not done twice, which is what this archive concluded about the two Catherine Mary Sophias.

Does the count come right
ELEVEN, WHICH IS WHAT THE 1903 REGISTRATION SAYS

Nine baptisms plus HENDRIK NICHOLAAS and RICHARD PETER — both named on their parents' death notices and in no register this archive can find — makes eleven. MARGARET MARY of the death notices is almost certainly MARGRITH LOUISA MARIA: it is her mother's name and there is no other candidate in the sibling group. Inferred from the count and the name, and marked as inferred.

22,059 RECORDS FOR FILM 008039088 — THE WHOLE INDEXED FILM
Which would have made weeks of hand-sweeping unnecessary, if it could be paged. IT CANNOT.

Can the film be paged out
NO — IT PAGES TO OFFSET 1000 AND THEN SILENTLY RETURNS PAGE ONE

At offset 1001 the API gives back the first page again. NO ERROR, NO WARNING, NO CHANGE IN THE REPORTED TOTAL: the response still says “results: 22059” and still says “index: 0”. AN UNCHECKED SWEEP WOULD HAVE RE-READ THE FIRST THOUSAND RECORDS TWENTY-TWO TIMES AND REPORTED THE FILM AS HOLDING 1,400 ENTRIES. Caught by comparing the first name at offset 0 against offset 1400 — identical — and bisecting to the edge. THE FOURTH UNDOCUMENTED BOUNDARY IN A WEEK, and the first that answers WRONGLY rather than emptily.

sets.g: The Vaalbank school file finished, and the Johannesburg directories priced out
sets.n: Closing the last two items that could be worked from here
rows: The remaining twenty-four Vaalbank documents
THE SCHOOL OUTLIVES THE REPUBLIC, AND DS BOOYSEN IS ON EXACTLY THREE OF THE FIFTY-FOUR

The 1899 and 1900 files are J.P. Louw alone — inspection reports, railway certificates for abroad, a declaration about the illness of the pupil JM ESTERHUIZEN, three free-boarding pupils leaving on 30 June, and then his own monthly salary certificates running to May 1900. NO FURTHER BOOYSEN APPEARS. And then the school simply continues: TED E600, “VAALBANK 116 SKOOL, LICHTENBURG SKOOLRAAD, STIGTING, 1905–1942”; TED E1954, establishments 1908–1937; a CLEANING ALLOWANCE for Vaalbank No. 116 in 1929 and 1937. THE FARM SCHOOL ON THIS FAMILY'S OWN GROUND RAN FOR AT LEAST FORTY-FOUR YEARS AND HAD A NUMBER.
yes
A detail worth a second look
A SCHOOL TRANSPORT ROUTE, VAALBANK TO KAFFERSKRAAL

TOD E13/26/71, “TRANSPORT SCHEMES. LICHTENBURG BOARD. VAALBANK – KAFFERSKRAAL”, 1939–1954. KAFFERSKRAAL IS THE POST OFFICE OF THE KWAGGAFONTEIN SCHOOL IN MARICO — the other farm school this archive found, forty years earlier. It may well be a different Kafferskraal; the name is common and Lichtenburg is not Marico. RECORDED AS A COINCIDENCE OF NAMES UNTIL SOMETHING SAYS OTHERWISE.
part
Johannesburg street directories, 1905–1935
NOT FREELY DIGITISED — IT IS A PURCHASE OR A LIBRARY

Longland's Johannesburg and Districts Directory exists for the 1890s and is sold commercially as a reproduction; the 1905–1935 run is not online free anywhere this archive can reach. The route is the Johannesburg City Library or a bookseller. NOT A SCREEN QUESTION, and open question 10 — whether the boys went to the mines — stays where it is. WHAT WOULD UNBLOCK IT: buying a reproduction, or a reader at the Johannesburg City Library. Neither is a search and both are David's to decide.

THERE IS STILL ONLY THE ONE, AND IT STILL BOUNCES

sandfdoc@mweb.co.za is the address on the Centre's own directory entries and on every guide that lists it, and it returns 550 relay access denied. WHAT IS LEFT IS THE TELEPHONE, (012) 339-4600, the Schweikert Building at 20 Visagie Street, and archive@dod.mil.za, which did not bounce and has not answered in six days. This is as far as this archive can take it from here.

sets.g: The gravestone collection swept, with the controls run first
sets.n: Two of the five surnames are simply not in it, and this time the zero can be trusted
rows: MOUNTJOY and DASCHNER in the Genealogical Society's gravestone data
NOUGHT AND NOUGHT — AND THE CONTROLS SAY IT IS REAL

BARRY returns 54, KOLBE 4, BOOYZEN 3. The database answers and answers a lot. A MONTH AGO THIS ARCHIVE WOULD HAVE WRITTEN “NO MOUNTJOY GRAVESTONES” AND MOVED ON; the number that makes that sentence mean anything is not nought, it is fifty-four.
no
KOLBE — four stones, three of them new
VOLKSRUST, UTRECHT AND NEW GELDERLAND

“Kolbe, GE — Concentration Camp cemetery, VOLKSRUST” — this archive knew a Kolbe died in that camp and NOW HAS THE INITIALS, which are two of the Commandant's three. “Van der Spuy, MH — Old Utrecht Cemetery, d. 13 August 1946” is MARGARET HARRIET born Kolbe, whose Natal estate NAB MSCE 1639/1946 was found the same afternoon — SHE NOW HAS A GRAVE AS WELL AS A FILE. And “Fourie, MD — New Gelderland, 29 September 1899 to 8 December 1979”, M.D. on a Kolbe-connected stone eighty years after Margaret Downing died.
yes
BOOYZEN — three stones, and they are one household
A WHOLE FAMILY IN ONE PRIVATE CEMETERY

Viljoen JCE (2 Jul 1807 – 11 Dec 1861), Viljoen BC (8 Jan 1807 – 25 Nov 1859) and Bezuidenhout JCE (30 Oct 1831 – 11 Jan 1904), all in the BEZUIDENHOUT FAMILY CEMETERY at Bezuidenhout Park, Johannesburg. That is JUDITH CORNELIA THERESIA BOOIJSEN — b3c4d5e6, baptised 16 August 1807 — WITH HER HUSBAND AND HER DAUGHTER. This archive had her stone and did not have the other two or know they were in the same ground.
yes
A position on what a memoir is worth, since two of them cost walls
A WITNESS, NOT A RECORD — AND THE TWO CLAIMS ARE NOT EQUAL

John Montgomery was recalling forty-five and forty-seven years back. The test being used: DOES THE MEMOIR CLAIM SOMETHING IT HAD NO REASON TO INVENT, AND DOES ANYTHING INDEPENDENT TOUCH IT? On KOOLSKOP something does — a library catalogue written from the papers calls Kolbe an LMS missionary, and the Kolbe page had already deduced a mission circuit from the children's birthplaces. Three lines, none aware of the others. ON THE 21ST DRAGOONS NOTHING DOES YET: he is in no name-catalogued discharge series at Kew, and that may be structural or may be a misremembered regiment. THE TWO ARE WRITTEN UP DIFFERENTLY ON THIS SITE FOR THAT REASON AND NOT BECAUSE ONE IS A BETTER STORY.

rows: The three Booyzens in the camps, read on the University of Cape Town's own pages
AND ONE OF THE THREE DID NOT DIE IN A CAMP

GERT JACOBUS BOOYZEN — “Master”, place of death JOHANNESBURG RC, aged 2, DIED IN CAMP: YES, cause “ziekte”, white, single, nationality TRANSVAAL, registration as child: yes. Farm RIETVALLEI, district MARICO. GERTRUIDA MAGDALENA BOOYZEN — “Ms”, place of death VEREENIGING RC, aged 19, DIED IN CAMP: YES, cause “ziekte”, with the note “OR IRENE RC”, so the camp itself is uncertain. Farm RIETVLEI, district HEIDELBERG. JAN GERHARDUS LODEWICUS BOOYZEN — aged 2, cause “ziekte”, and DIED IN CAMP: NO, with NO CAMP AND NO FARM RECORDED AT ALL. OPEN QUESTION 3 ON THIS SITE LISTS ALL THREE AS THOUGH THEY WERE THE SAME KIND OF RECORD. They are not.
yes
Where those records come from
RS 25 TRANSVAAL DEATH LISTS, NATIONAL ARCHIVES, PRETORIA

The database names its own source on every page. IT CONFIRMS THE CAVEAT THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY PUBLISHED ABOUT IT — these are DEATH LISTS, so the database records who died far better than who was interned and walked out, and an absence from it is much weaker than a presence. And the cause of death on all three is the same word: ZIEKTE. Illness. The lists recorded no diagnosis.

The 1925 voters' roll entries for Jacobus Nicolas and John Barry Booyzen
THE YEAR IS FREE AND THE ADDRESS IS NOT

Both are on the roll for VOTING YEAR 1925. Employment, address, race, town, division, voting district, province and voting number are all behind “Sign up to view”. THE ADDRESS WAS THE ENTIRE POINT OF THE ITEM: both men are on the list of six bound estate files now with a private researcher in Pretoria, and a street and a district would tell her where to look. A SUBSCRIPTION WOULD BUY EXACTLY THE FIELD THAT MATTERS, which is worth knowing precisely rather than in general.

The Civil Death and Unconfirmed Death databases
TWO MEN THIS ARCHIVE DID NOT HOLD

HENRY JOHN BOOYZEN, born 14 FEBRUARY 1929, died 29 MARCH 1966 — and this archive holds a HENRY JAMES Booyzen born 12 August 1887. A different man and a later one, and the difference is one forename. MARUIS BOOYZEN, born 28 January 1963, died 2 May 2011. Neither is placed. Recorded as names with dates and nothing else, which is what they are.
part
The Old Voter Rolls and estate finders as tools
THEY ARE BROWSE TOOLS, NOT INDEXES

Old Voter Rolls takes a TOWN and lists which rolls exist; the Cape and Transvaal estate finders take a REFERENCE and resolve it to a film. NONE OF THEM SEARCHES A NAME — the name search is the single AIO box, which this archive has already run. Useful for turning a reference into an image, useless for finding a person, and worth writing down so the distinction is not rediscovered.

sets.g: The Cape estate index for Mountjoy, a surname sweep abandoned, and the 1931 six given parents
sets.n: Three roadmap items worked in one pass at NAAIRS
rows: MOUNTJOY in the Cape depot (KAB)
FORTY-TWO, AND THE 1834 MEMORIAL IS REAL

KAB CO 3972 ref 17, “MEMORIALS RECEIVED. THE WIDOW OF J MOUNTJOY. REQUESTING REMISSION OF A FINE”, 1834 — already on the errands list and now confirmed present in the index rather than taken from a note. Also MOOC 6/9/15220 (JAMES JOHN MOUNTJOY, 1948), MOOC 6/9/16573 (BURGER, WILHELMINA LOUISA, née MOUNTJOY — the bride of a 1901 marriage found last week in the newspaper transcriptions) and MOOC 6/9/16323 (NEPGEN, ANNIE LOUISA, née MOUNTJOY). AND A WHOLE OTHER MOUNTJOY FAMILY: labour agents and traders in the Transkei — Lusikisiki, Bizana, Mnyameni, Lupatana — from the 1920s to the 1960s, with a Mountjoy Estates (Pty) Ltd registered in 1934. NOT THIS FAMILY SO FAR AS ANYTHING SHOWS.
yes
DOWNING as a bare surname across all depots
552 DOCUMENTS — NOT A SEARCH

Downing is an ordinary English surname and the first thirty returns contain no Kolbe, Booyzen, Barry or Mountjoy at all. THE PAIRING IS WHAT WORKS AND THE PAIRING WAS ALREADY RUN: KOLBE AND DOWNING returns sixteen, and those sixteen are where the four generations came from. Recorded so that nobody runs the bare sweep again expecting something.
void
The parents of the six Kolbes who applied to a Free State court together in 1931
GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE, d. 1905, AND HESTER JACOBA JACOMINA LOUW

VAB MHG K1431: “KOLBE, GEORGE AUGUSTUS. EGGENOTE HESTER JACOBA JACOMINA (GEBORE LOUW)”, 1905. VAB MHG 27114: her own estate, 1935. AND VAB MHG 1/2/1/1 KS3: “BOEDEL ONDER KURATORSKAP” — HER ESTATE PUT UNDER CURATORSHIP IN 1905, which is what happens when there are minor children. THE MECHANISM THAT NAMES THEM IS A FORENAME: one of the six is JACOBUS WYNAND LOUW KOLBE, and LOUW is his mother's maiden name; another is GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE, which is his father's. The 1931 application is twenty-six years after the father's death and four before the mother's. INFERRED, NOT PROVED — the index does not list heirs, and the file will.
part
Whether that George Augustus Kolbe connects to the 1820 Settler
NOT SHOWN, AND NOT ASSUMED

The Settler's name was carried by at least one son and repeats through the Free State Kolbes for a century. A George Augustus Kolbe dying at Bloemfontein in 1905 is the right family of names in the right province, AND THAT IS ALL IT IS. This archive has spent a week refusing to adopt thirty-one plausible children from a tree and is not going to adopt a grandfather from a forename.
no

sets.g: The memoir did not need reading, and the ship did
sets.n: An item closed by argument rather than by work, and a voyage found by searching for the vessel
rows: John Montgomery's serialised memoir, read entire
UNNECESSARY, AND THE REASONING IS THE POINT

It runs through The Friend across 1868, 1869 and 1870 under two titles — “Forty-five years ago” and “Fifty years ago: A Few Episodes in the Lives of the British Settlers of 1820” — and it has already produced the Koolskop mission school and the 21st Dragoons. BOTH CAME OUT OF SWEEPING A SURNAME ACROSS THE WHOLE COLLECTION, AND THOSE SWEEPS ARE DONE: Kolbe returns 43 documents and Mountjoy six, across every paper in the archive, and KOOLSKOP APPEARS EXACTLY ONCE IN THE WHOLE COLLECTION — in the passage already read. Reading a long memoir to find what a name search has already found is work that looks like diligence.
void
What the 1870 instalments actually are
THE SALEM PARTY, NOT OWEN'S

The 1870 series carries a complete list of the SALEM party of 1820 settlers, sent to Montgomery by W.E. Prynn on 31 December 1869 with asterisks against those still living. VALUABLE AND NOT THIS FAMILY'S: George Augustus Kolbe came out in OWEN'S party. Recorded so nobody reads the list hopefully.
no
The Nautilus, searched as a ship rather than as a person
A FIRST-HAND ACCOUNT OF THIS FAMILY'S OWN CROSSING

JOHN PENNY MANDY led another party on the same vessel and wrote home to his mother in Kent. In a letter of January 1820 he describes THE NAUTILUS DISASTER IN THE DOWNS — a day out of Gravesend, at anchor in the Queen's Channel: “it came on to blow tremendously hard, the sea running mountains high… men, women and children all mixed together, tumbling over one another”; the sea broke into the cabin windows; THE SHIP STRUCK ON THE SANDS and “even the sailors seemed panic struck”. Then a second storm of three days with three tons of water in the forepart. NOT ABOUT THIS FAMILY AND ON THE SAME DECK: a boy four days short of seventeen and a girl of sixteen, both of whom had sworn they were older, were somewhere in that cabin.
yes
And it confirms the dates from a second direction
ALGOA BAY, APRIL 1820, AND A BIRTH AT SEA

Mandy writes from Algoa Bay on 20 APRIL 1820; this archive has the Nautilus there on 14 April. WILLIAM NAUTILUS MANDY was born aboard on 1 MARCH 1820, “in latitude 18 degrees, longitude six degrees”, a fortnight short of Table Bay and named for the ship; he died at Lushington Valley in 1887. THE ORIGINAL LETTERS WENT TO THE ALBANY MUSEUM AT GRAHAMSTOWN AND WERE DESTROYED IN A FIRE IN THE 1920s — what survives is a descendant's copy, printed in a newspaper in 1970.
part

sets.g: Natal opened, the Transvaal swept for the other surnames, and a link this archive nearly invented
sets.n: NAB had never been searched — it had only ever been asked for six references somebody else found
rows: CK BARRY, WAKKERSTROOM — “MR. GS KOLBE ASKS TO BE SUPPLIED WITH A COPY OF THE ROAD BOARD LAW”, 1908
HE IS CYRIL KERSHAW BARRY, AND HE IS AN ATTORNEY

A Barry and a Kolbe in one sentence, in the district whose Kolbes this archive has spent weeks trying to attach to the Settler — and this archive holds three Barrys carrying KOLBE AS A FORENAME. It read for about ten minutes like a fourth. FOUR FURTHER DOCUMENTS SETTLE IT: he asks about a Commissioner of Oaths at Wakkerstroom, enquires about a certificate of domicile for MAHOMED MAMOOJEE MOTALA OF LADYSMITH, forwards quitrent on behalf of MR MOLL, and writes on the division of ground in Natal. THAT IS A COUNTRY SOLICITOR'S WEEK AND G.S. KOLBE IS A CLIENT. Set down at length because it was a good mistake to almost make.
no
KOLBE in NAB
THIRTY-NINE — AND TWO OF THEM CONFIRM A MARRIAGE THIS ARCHIVE HAD ONLY FROM BAPTISMS

MSCE 8509/1923, “KOLBE, ELIZABETH JOHANNA (BORN DU TOIT), S/S FREDERICK FORTUNATUS”, and MSCE 15161/1929, his own, cross-referenced to hers. The Settler's tenth child and his wife, BOTH THEIR ESTATES IN NATAL. And MSCE 21335/1934 gives HENDRIK JOHANNES HOFMEYR KOLBE — one of the two men on the unsent Pietermaritzburg letter — A WIFE: Johanna Maria, born Potgieter.
yes
MOUNTJOY in NAB
NINE, AND A SECOND BARKLY EAST WOMAN NOBODY HAD

MSCE 581/1973, “SHOOTER, MATHILDA ELIZABETH, BORN MOUNTJOY, BORN IN BARKLY EAST” — alongside Christian Mountjoy already on the Pietermaritzburg list. TWO PEOPLE LEAVING BARKLY EAST FOR NATAL IS A PATTERN. Also BOTHMA, WRAY, born MOUNTJOY, born in KOKSTAD — the bride of a 1957 marriage found last week in the newspaper transcriptions, now with a birthplace.
yes
BOOYZEN in NAB
FOUR, AND THE OLDEST IS 1846

NAB RSC 1/5/3 46/1846: “ILLIQUID CASE. PETRUS GERHARDUS BOOYZEN VERSUS DAVID SCHALK VAN DER MERWE.” THE OLDEST BOOYZEN DOCUMENT THIS ARCHIVE HAS FOUND OUTSIDE THE CAPE — and the defendant's name is the one this site spent yesterday proving is a van der Merwe name that entered the Booyzen line by marriage. NO CONNECTION IS CLAIMED: Petrus Gerhardus is not a name in this archive, and a Booyzen in Natal in 1846 is likelier a trekker family. Also MSCE 4064/1974, BOOYZEN, NICOLAAS THEODORUS, BORN IN WAKKERSTROOM — a Booyzen born in the Kolbe district.
part
DASCHNER, the whole surname
TWELVE IN THE TRANSVAAL, NONE IN NATAL

WILLIAM HERMAN DASCHNER, d. 1963, NOW HAS A WIFE — MILDRED. A HEINRICH DASCHNER died in 1969 and the index marks him CHILD. And a HENRY JAMES DASCHNER appears twice, which is the Barry and Booyzen forename string arriving on a fourth surname by way of Catherine Mary Sophia. SMALL ENOUGH TO WORK ENTIRE, AND NOW WORKED ENTIRE.
yes
MOUNTJOY in TAB
THIRTY-NINE, INCLUDING A FARM OF THAT NAME

TAB SS 2932 R8960/91: the Registrar of Deeds sending title for the farms “MOUNTJOY”, Smaldeel, Bloemhof, Krausberg and Gossard, 1891. TAB PM 29 66/6/1907: “LANDS — MOUNTJOY AND PHILLAMORE'S OCCUPATION — RUSTENBURG DISTRICT”, which is this archive's own district. And W MOUNTJOY'S APPLICATION TO CAPTURE OSTRICH CHICKS, 1906.
yes
KOLBE in the education series
ONE, AND IT IS AT WAKKERSTROOM

TAB OD OR3052/99: declarations from the school at MARTINUS WESSELSTROOM — the old name for Wakkerstroom — “ONDERTEEKEND DOOR DE HEEREN GA KOLBE EN FRANCOIS L…”. A George Augustus Kolbe signing for a school commission in 1899. BARRY in the same series returns nothing.
yes
The farms put through the education series
ABANDONED AS VOID, WITH ONE KEPT

BRAKFONTEIN RETURNS 77, KOEDOESFONTEIN 188, GOEDEHOOP 41 — among the commonest farm names in the country, and the results are other people's schools in other districts. A FARM-NAME SWEEP WITHOUT A SURNAME IS NOT A SEARCH. One is worth keeping: OD OR150/95, “CAB MEYER, KOEDOESFONTEIN, WYK ZWARTRUGGENS, RUSTENBURG”, is unmistakably this archive's Koedoesfontein, where Hendrik Stefanus Booijsen died in 1908. IT HAD A SCHOOL IN 1895 AND NO BOOYZEN IS ANYWHERE ON ITS PAPERS.

sets.g: The Kew catalogue searched before the Kew letter was written — and it changed the letter
sets.n: The first British catalogue this archive has ever put any of its people to
rows: MOUNTJOY, MONTJOY, MOUNTJOYE and MUNTJOY across the WO series at The National Archives
TWO MONTJOYS IN THE DISCHARGE SERIES, AND NEITHER IS HIM

WO 97/1147/67, JOHN MONTJOY, born BARNSTAPLE, Devonshire, 56th Foot. WO 121/44/280, WILLIAM MONTJOY alias WILLIAM MOUNTJOY, born DUBLIN, 16th and 60th Foot. Nothing else in WO 97, WO 119, WO 120, WO 121 or WO 25 under any of the four spellings.
no
Is that a negative or an indexing gap
A NEGATIVE, AND THE CONTROL SAYS SO

THE CATALOGUE INDEXES THE REGIMENT AS “21ST DRAGOONS (LIGHT)” AND NOT AS “21ST LIGHT DRAGOONS” — which is the form the newspaper used and the form this archive had been writing. Searched the right way it returns 790 documents, NINETY-FIVE OF THEM WO 97 IN A SINGLE PAGE, plus entries in WO 119, WO 121 and WO 25. So the series is name-catalogued, the regiment is in it, and he is not. ONE WORD ORDER WAS THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A REAL RECORD AND A NIL RETURN, which is the fourth time in a week this archive has met that shape.
yes
Why he is absent, most likely
WO 97 AND WO 121 ARE PENSIONERS' PAPERS

A man discharged locally at the Cape who never claimed a Chelsea or Kilmainham pension leaves no discharge document in either. THE REGIMENT WAS IN THE CAPE COLONY FROM 1806 AND LEFT IN SEPTEMBER 1817 (this row said 1816 until 17 September, when five London papers dated the embarkation for India); HE MARRIED AT GRAAFF-REINET IN MARCH 1817. So he was discharged at the Cape and stayed behind when it sailed — which is exactly the kind of man these series do not hold.
part
What to read instead
WO 12/1450 — THE MUSTERS AND PAY LISTS FOR THE 21ST, 1816–17 (this row said WO 12/1430 until 17 Sep)

CORRECTED 17 SEPTEMBER. WO 12/1430 is the 20TH AND 21ST DRAGOONS FOR 1867–1868 — fifty years late and the re-raised regiment, not this one. The 21st Light Dragoons has its own continuous run: WO 12/1446 (1805–06), 1447 (1807–09), 1448 (1810–12), 1449 (1813–15), WO 12/1450 (1816–17), 1451 (1818), 1452 (1819–20). Not name-indexed; they have to be read. A man's disappearance from a muster DATES HIS DISCHARGE, and WO 12/1450 alone covers the window.
part
And what that did to the letter
REWROTE IT BEFORE IT WAS SENT

The errand as this archive raised it this morning was “WO 97 for the 21st Light Dragoons”. THE LETTER NOW ASKS NOBODY TO LOOK IN WO 97. It sets out what was searched and what the control showed, asks whether the pensioner reading is right, and names the piece it believes it needs. A LETTER THAT ASKS AN ARCHIVIST TO REPEAT A SEARCH ANYONE CAN RUN FROM AUSTRALIA IS A WASTE OF SOMEBODY'S MORNING.
yes

sets.g: The Free State depot swept properly — and a library catalogue makes the Settler a missionary
sets.n: VAB had been opened twice in this project's life, both times for one reference
rows: MSB751, SA Library, Cape Town — found while searching KOLBE AND DOWNING
“GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE … 1820 SETTLER, MISSIONARY … LMS MISSIONARY”

A library manuscript collection, not an archive file: “GA KOLBE COLLECTION. Donated by Dr Jean Griffiths, Somerset West, 1985. Photocopy, 4 pages.” IT CORROBORATES A MEMORY THIS ARCHIVE PUBLISHED THE SAME MORNING AS AN INFERENCE — John Montgomery's recollection of a Bushman mission school at Koolskop about 1824. An old man's memoir in a Bloemfontein newspaper and a manuscript donated to a Cape Town library in 1985 have nothing to do with each other AND THEY AGREE. It also settles the trade: the settler roll said CHEMIST, the catalogue says PHARMACIST, the obituary describes a medical practice. One man, one trade, and the missionary work is the part nobody had.
yes
And the other half of the same catalogue line
A LETTER FROM HIS FATHER IN LONDON, 23 AUGUST 1830

“LETTER, 1830 AUG. 23, FROM JOHAN KOLBE, LONDON, TO HIS SON, GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE ON HIS ORDINATION.” THE TWO MEN WROTE TO EACH OTHER AND THE LETTER SURVIVES. This archive has spent a fortnight trying to connect the tailor of Conduit Street to the settler of Colesberg through directories, censuses and an obituary, and has been beaten by a quota, a bot check and an empty shelf. A letter from London in 1830 is very likely to carry an address at its head — which is the exact question the Brunswick Square muddle turns on. IT IS A PHOTOCOPY, and the catalogue does not say where the original is.
yes
MCCABE in VAB
THIRTEEN, AND THREE OF THEM MATTER

VAB MHG C129: “MCCABE, FRANCIS. EGGENOTES 1) MARIA PETRONELLA ELISABETHA ANTOINETTA RAATH EN 2) ANNA (GEBORE VAN DER MERWE)”, 1872 — HE HAD A FIRST WIFE AND SHE HAS A NAME. VAB 1/3/1/12 BC11: “MCCABE, FRANCIS. INSOLVENTE BOEDEL”, remark “BEVAT GEEN STERFKENNIS NIE” — THE LANDDROST OF BLOEMFONTEIN DIED INSOLVENT, and the index says outright the file holds no death notice, which saves somebody a wasted morning. And M777 now reads in full: “EGGENOTE JOHN GHERSON ELEASAR KOLBE EN FRANCIS MCCABE” — the remarriage is in the archives, not only in a newspaper.
yes
The Kolbe–McCabe marriage this archive had flagged as possibly coincidence
IT IS NOT A COINCIDENCE

IT STOPS BEING UNANSWERABLE AND BECOMES AN ERRAND AT KEW

His death notice answers “names of the parents of the deceased” with NOT KNOWN. rows: The letter to the National Archives in Pretoria, 12 September — six Transvaal estate files
ANSWERED. “ALL THE ESTATE FILES YOU ARE REQUESTING ARE BOUND FILES.”

Ms Mavis Xaba, Archivist Assistant, Reading Room, NARSSA: “Unfortunately, we are therefore unable to scan these files and provide complete digital copies by email.” THAT IS NOT A REFUSAL, IT IS A PHYSICAL FACT ABOUT THE RECORD — the paper is sewn into volumes and will not lie on a scanner. It explains a great deal about what has and has not been filmed, and it retires an assumption this archive has been making for weeks: that the obstacle was willingness or staff time. She put a private researcher who specialises in estate files on copy. ENGAGING HER IS THE USER'S DECISION AND THE USER'S MONEY, and this archive does not spend either.
part
And whether any of the six references was wrong
SHE CORRECTED NONE OF THEM — INCLUDING MHG 52653

The letter singled out TAB MHG 52653 (BOOYZEN, JACOBUS NICHOLS, 1923) as the one file of the six that could not be found on microfilm at all, and asked to be told if the reference needed correcting. THE REPLY SAYS “ALL THE ESTATE FILES YOU ARE REQUESTING ARE BOUND FILES” AND NAMES NO EXCEPTION. Weak evidence — a general sentence is not a file-by-file check — but it is the first thing this archive has had suggesting that reference is real.
part
G2G — does de Villiers & Pama (1981) still place Petrus Jacobus under JAN?
“YES. b3c4d7 b. 21 SEPT 1788 UNDER JAN b3c4.”

Riël Smit, who owns the 1981 edition this archive has never seen. THAT WAS THE LAST ESCAPE ROUTE. The standing objection was that a revision can move a man, and if Pama had relocated Petrus Jacobus the 1876 death notice would stand unopposed. IT DID NOT.
yes
Is there any marriage of a Gerhardus Lodewicus to a Magdalena de Beer?
A CAPE GENEALOGIST WENT LOOKING AND FOUND NONE

Pieter van Zyl: “I searched for a marriage between a Gerhardus Lodewicus and Magdalena de Beer but could not find one.” The pairing on line 3 of the 1876 Sterfkennis exists in no marriage record anybody has been able to produce. THE MOTHER ON THAT LINE AGREES WITH THE BOOK EXACTLY; the father does not.
no
Van Zyl's guess from memory — that a CHILD of Petrus Jacobus carried the name
HE IS RIGHT, AND THE CHILD IS NINE LINES LOWER ON THE SAME SHEET

Line 3 of Notice 678: parents, “GERTHARDUS LÖDEWIKUS BOOIJSEN” and “Magdalena de Beer”. Line 12 of Notice 678: eight children, all of age, the fifth being “JAN GERTHARDUS LODEWIKUS BOOIJSEN”. THE NAME IN THE PARENTS' BOX IS THE BACK HALF OF A SON'S NAME, IN ONE CLERK'S HAND, ON ONE PAGE — and the half that was dropped is JAN, which is the name the book gives the father. A grandson named for his grandfather is the ordinary thing in this family, and this archive has a page proving it.
yes
Who was doing the remembering
HENDRIK STEFANUS, THE SEVENTH CHILD, WHO SIGNED IT

H. S. Booijsen countersigned the form beside the veldkornet, four lines below his own name in the children's list. Born about 1828. His grandfather Jan married in 1770 and remarried in 1793, and van Zyl puts his death more than forty years before 1876. HE WAS WRITING THE NAME OF A MAN HE HAD ALMOST CERTAINLY NEVER MET, about a father who was eighty-eight.
yes
Is the pedigree spine being moved to Jan
NO, AND THIS IS DELIBERATE

Everything against Gerthardus Lodewikus is SECONDARY. De Villiers is a printed genealogy of 1893; Pama's revision agreeing with it is one book agreeing with its own earlier edition, not two sources agreeing. Against it stands a PRIMARY document signed by a son. THIS ARCHIVE DOES NOT LET A BOOK OVERRULE A PAGE BECAUSE THE BOOK IS TIDIER. Jan Booijsen is entered as INFERRED, not documented, and the chart still shows Gerthardus Lodewikus at the top, marked open.
part
What would actually end it
THE BAPTISM REGISTER ENTRY OF 21 SEPTEMBER 1788

DE VILLIERS IS NOT A SOURCE, HE IS AN INDEX TO ONE. His entry for Petrus Jacobus was compiled from the Dutch Reformed doopregister, and that entry names the father in a contemporary hand, written within days of the birth, by somebody with no reason to be confused. Graaff-Reinet, Drakenstein and Stellenbosch for September 1788, in that order — b3c4 Jan was a burgher at Drakenstein and the family is at Graaff-Reinet by 1812. FIRST ITEM ON THE ERRANDS PAGE.
part

sets.g: Parts 2 and 3 of the Cape genealogies, downloaded at last — and the name David Schalk has a source
sets.n: Riël Smit posted the links on 14 September. This archive read Part 1 and forgot the other two.
rows: archive.org — geslachtregister02devi and geslachtregister03devi
BOTH VOLUMES, FULL TEXT, IN UNDER A MINUTE

They had been sitting behind a link in a forum answer for a day. The whole of this run took one download and some counting. THE COST OF NOT GOING BACK FOR THE SECOND HALF OF SOMETHING SOMEBODY HANDED YOU.
yes
KOLBE in de Villiers
A483 — AND IT IS SOMEBODY ELSE ENTIRELY

“Carel Frederik Kolbe, VAN ANHALT DESSAU, burger te Kaapstad, gehuwd 6 Juni 1762 met Maria Magdalena de Wens”, with seven children baptised 1763–1773; volume 3 confirms the son Jacobus's 1799 marriage from the Paulsen side. A GERMAN KOLBE FAMILY WAS AT THE CAPE FIFTY-EIGHT YEARS BEFORE THE 1820 SETTLER LANDED, and it is not his — his father was a London tailor and he came out on the settler ships. Set down deliberately, as the trap it is.
no
ANNA MARIA VAN DER MERWE — who she was
BAPTISED 5 OCTOBER 1788, AND SIX SIBLINGS

Volume 2, van der Merwe: “(e) 3 WILLEM, gedoopt 30 September 1764, burger te Stellenbosch, gehuwd 7 November 1784 met HESTER MARIA VAN DER MERWE — (f) 1 Johanna Catharina 1787; 2 ANNA MARIA, GEDOOPT 5 OCTOBER 1788, GEHUWD MET PETRUS JACOBUS BOOIJSEN; 3 DAVID SCHALK, gedoopt 10 October 1790; 4 Hendrina Magdalena 1792; 5 Hester Maria 1793; 6 Hendrik Petrus Jacobus 1796.” SHE HAS BEEN A NAME ON ONE BAPTISM FOR THE WHOLE OF THIS PROJECT.
yes
Two babies, fourteen days apart
HE 21 SEPTEMBER 1788, SHE 5 OCTOBER 1788

Volume 1 page 78 for him, volume 2 for her. The same author writing consistently with himself, which is worth exactly that and no more — but it is the first date of any kind this archive has had for her.
yes
Her parents — against WikiTree
THEY DISAGREE, AND THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES BOTH

WikiTree makes her a daughter of DAVID SCHALK VAN DER MERWE and ANNA ELIZABETH LOUW, born 1785. De Villiers makes her a daughter of WILLEM VAN DER MERWE and HESTER MARIA VAN DER MERWE, baptised 1788. BOTH CANNOT BE RIGHT AND NEITHER IS BEING ADOPTED. On the tree's version David Schalk is her FATHER; on the book's he is her BROTHER. A CONCLUSION THAT HOLDS UNDER EITHER READING IS THE ONLY KIND THIS ARCHIVE GETS TO KEEP.
part
Count the name across all three volumes
ONCE IN PART 1, FIFTEEN TIMES IN PART 2

Part 1 holds the entire BOOIJSEN genealogy, and the string “David Schalk” occurs in it EXACTLY ONCE — “David Schalk, gedoopt 4 Januari 1807”, which is our man, the child born the year after a van der Merwe married into the line. Of the fifteen in Part 2, THIRTEEN ARE INSIDE THE VAN DER MERWE SECTION, generation after generation: 1738, 1739, 1761, 1787, 1790, 1791, 1797, 1800, 1804. DAVID SCHALK IS A VAN DER MERWE NAME and this archive can now say so with a count behind it.
yes
Adriana Christina Viljoen — who she was
PROBABLY HIS FIRST COUSIN

Volume 3, VILLION thans VILJOEN: “(e) 12 HERCULES ALBERTUS, gedoopt 30 Maart 1777, burger te Graaff-Reinet, GEHUWD 26 FEBRUARI 1797 MET MAGDALENA BOOIJSEN”, whose seventh child is “ADRIANA CHRISTINA, GEDOOPT 19 AUGUSTUS 1810”. Magdalena Booijsen is b3c4d6 — the SISTER of Petrus Jacobus. Eighteen in 1828, right district, right name. NOT PROVED: de Villiers gives her NO HUSBAND, and the 3 November 1828 Cradock date is itself only on WikiTree. The Cradock marriage register would close it.
part
The Booijsen–Viljoen marriages of 1797
A BROTHER AND A SISTER MARRIED A SISTER AND A BROTHER, THREE MONTHS APART

Magdalena Booijsen (b3c4d6) married Hercules Albertus Viljoen on 26 FEBRUARY 1797. Her brother Jan Jonathan Booijsen (b3c4d5) married his sister Judith Cornelia Theresia Viljoen on 28 MAY 1797. Two households became one twice over in a single year, and thirty-one years later a son of the third sibling married a daughter of the first.
yes
b3c4d5e6, resolved last week from a gravestone, explained this week
SHE HAS HER MOTHER'S THREE NAMES ENTIRE

Jan Jonathan Booijsen and Judith Cornelia Theresia Viljoen's sixth child is “JUDITH CORNELIA THERESIA, gedoopt 16 Augustus 1807”. The same mechanism as David Schalk, in the same generation, in the house next door: A DISTINCTIVE NAME ENTERS THIS SURNAME BY MARRIAGE AND IS HANDED STRAIGHT DOWN.
yes
MOUNTJOY, DOWNING, WERDMULLER, SLEER in de Villiers
NOT THERE AT ALL

Zero occurrences of Mountjoy, Montjoy, Downing, Werdmuller or Sleer across all three volumes. De Villiers recorded the OLD CAPE families — the Dutch, German and French of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. THE BRITISH AND THE 1820 SETTLERS ARE SIMPLY OUT OF SCOPE, which is a fact about the book and not about the families, and is the reason half this archive will never be found in it.
no
Google Books, to chase the London tailor into a directory
BLOCKED — QUOTA ZERO WITHOUT A KEY

books.googleapis.com returns HTTP 429, “quota_limit_value: 0”, for anonymous callers. Item 9 — whether John Godloff Kolbe of the 1844 obituary was at Brunswick Square or at Conduit Street — is not closed and needs a different route. ONE THING DID COME OUT OF IT: a list of 234 London master tailors who met at the Freemasons' Tavern on 22 December 1799 over the Combination Act, printed in The Times of 27 January 1800, includes “KOLBE, JOHN, 18, BROAD-STREET, SOHO”. Right trade, right city, right age, and Soho was the German quarter. NOT CLAIMED, because a John Kolbe in London is not yet this John Kolbe.
blocked

sets.g: The Free State papers, worked properly — McCabe named, the farm placed, and a son of the twelve
sets.n: Forty-three Kolbe hits in the newspaper transcriptions, read one by one instead of skimmed
rows: Who was McCabe — the surname the Free State estate index files the Commandant's widow under
FRANCIS McCABE, LANDDROST OF BLOEMFONTEIN

The Friend, 29 February 1872, with an obituary under it: son of DR McCABE, a Staff-Assistant Surgeon attached to the British Army on the Cape Frontier, born at one of the military posts in what is now British Kaffraria on 29 SEPTEMBER 1817; “married his second wife about ten months since — THE WIDOW OF THE LATE COMMANDANT J.G.E. KOLBE, OF KAFIRBERG, NEAR THIS TOWN”; died suddenly of heart disease on 23 February 1872, aged 54. THIS ARCHIVE HAS BEEN SAYING FOR DAYS THAT IT DID NOT KNOW WHO McCABE WAS. He was the town's own magistrate.
yes
How long the second marriage lasted
ABOUT FIFTEEN MONTHS

Married about April 1871, widowed 23 February 1872. She had been widowed on 3 April 1868 with twelve children, and she outlived the second husband by twenty-four years. HIS OBITUARY COUNTS BOTH FAMILIES: “four sons and two daughters, BESIDES A LARGE FAMILY OF STEP-CHILDREN”. For about eleven months there were eighteen children attached to one household.
yes
How he died
A CART INTO A SLUIT, ON THE ANNIVERSARY OF THE STATE'S INDEPENDENCE

He had spent 23 February superintending the burghers' annual target shooting for the government prize. At 5:15 he set off by spring-cart with four horses, Adjutant van Rensburg of the Free State Artillery and a servant, for the Diamond Fields, meaning to sleep at his own farm UITVLUGT on the Modder River. At half past seven, in deceptive moonlight, ONE HOUR'S RIDE SHORT OF THE FARM OF MR G.F. ENSLIN, the cart went into a sluit washed out by the rains. G.F. ENSLIN IS ALREADY IN THIS ARCHIVE — he placed the 1863 notice saying Maria Elizabeth Kolbe had died intestate. Here he is a landmark on a road at night.
yes
Any of the twelve children, by name
ONE — “JOHN KOLBE, JUN.”

Free State criminal court, reported in The Friend in the second half of 1869: a horse thief pleaded guilty to driving off, in October 1868, from the farm SPRINGFIELD, WARD UPPER MODDER-RIVER, DISTRICT BLOEMFONTEIN, a black mare and foal belonging to “ANNA JACOBA VAN DER MERWE, WIDOW OF LATE J.G.E. KOLBE”, a blue schimmel mare and foal belonging to “JOHN KOLBE, JUN.”, and a chestnut riding horse belonging to “JEPHTS, A MAN OF COLOR, NOW RESIDING AT LEEUWBERG”. Six months after the death, a son is holding stock in his own right beside his mother. AND A MAN WHO WOULD OTHERWISE BE IN NO DOCUMENT AT ALL IS NAMED IN THE SAME SENTENCE, WITH PROPERTY OF HIS OWN.
yes
Where the farm actually was
ABOUT TWO HOURS' RIDE FROM BLOEMFONTEIN

The Friend, 13 January 1870, an auction advertisement dated Bloemfontein 30 November 1869: “The farm, WILDEBEESTKOOI, ADJOINING THE FARM LEEUBERG, THE PROPERTY OF THE LATE J.G.E. KOLBE, ABOUT TWO HOURS RIDE FROM THE TOWN OF BLOEMFONTEIN.” THIS ARCHIVE PINNED LEEUWBERG AT FAURESMITH TWO DAYS AGO, 130 KM AWAY, AND PUBLISHED THE PIN WITH ITS OWN OBJECTION ATTACHED. The objection was right. Withdrawn to /corrections/ and the pin moved. Kafferberg, Kaalspruit, Leeuberg, Wildebeestkooi and Springfield are one neighbourhood.
yes
What the Settler did before Colesberg existed
HE KEPT A MISSION SCHOOL FOR BUSHMEN ON THE GROUND THE TOWN WAS LAID OUT ON

The Friend, first half of 1869, “FORTY-FIVE YEARS AGO, by John MONTGOMERY, Founder of Burghersdorp”, describing a journey from Cradock about 1824: “I continued my journey towards the Orange River, BY KOOLSKOP, WHERE THE FATHER OF THE LATE LAMENTED COMMANDANT KOLBE CONDUCTED A BUSHMEN MISSION SCHOOL, AND WHICH IS NOW COLESBERG.” Colesberg was laid out in 1830. RECORDED AS AN INFERENCE: Montgomery is recalling forty-five years back and names the man only as somebody's father. It is also specific, and from a man who founded a town in the same district.
part
A fourth public office for the Commandant
FOREMAN OF THE JURY, BLOEMFONTEIN, 1866

A forgery trial before Mr van Soelen — the same official who spoke at Kolbe's graveside two years later. “The jury, through their foreman, MR. J.G.B. KOLBE, OF KAFFERBERG, brought in a verdict of Not Guilty.” The initials are printed J.G.B. for J.G.E., in his own town's paper, in his own lifetime.
yes
A grandson
“LITTLE JANNIE”, TEN YEARS OLD, KILLED BY LIGHTNING IN 1884 — FATHER UNCERTAIN

“The eldest son of Mr. John KOLBE, ‘little Jannie’, a promising youth ten years old, was struck dead by the electric fluid on his father's farm FIVE HOURS TO THE NORTHWARD OF BLOEMFONTEIN.” The Natal Witness index carries the same death and names the father GEORGE. TWO PAPERS, TWO FATHERS. If the John of 1884 is the John Kolbe junior of 1868, this is the Commandant's grandson, and this archive is not going to decide that on a preference.
part
KOLBE-BOOYSEN — the compound the Name page called a tree oddity
IT IS A HOUSEHOLD IN PORT ELIZABETH, AND IT IS IN PRINT TWICE

Eastern Province Herald, 16 October 1944: “SAWTELLE – KOLBY-BOOYSEN. The engagement has been announced between LEVINA (FINNIE), only daughter of Mr and Mrs D. KOLBE-BOOYSEN, of Port Elizabeth, to Raymond Patrick, only son of Mrs D. Sawtelle, of Cambridge, England.” And 19 April 1945: “KOLBE-BOOYSEN – KRUGER… Hilda, only daughter of Lieut. and Mrs F. Kruger of Heidelburg, Transvaal, to WILLIAM (S.A.A.F.), son of Mr and Mrs D. KOLBE-BOOYSEN, of Port Elizabeth.” D IS DAVID — David Kolbe Booyzen, married Maria Jacoba Smit 1921. A TOWN AND TWO CHILDREN. And the headline spells it KOLBY and the body KOLBE, four words apart.
yes
The rest of the forty-three
MOSTLY SOMEBODY ELSE, AND SET DOWN AS SUCH

A Kolbe girl of eleven drowned in a dam in the HANTAM district in 1874, saving a Hottentot girl who also drowned; Rev. F.W. KOLBE of the Paarl on a subscription list; Dr Kolbe the editor of the S.A. Catholic Magazine, ill in the Transkei in 1899; a watch-repair suit at Grahamstown in 1872; a Kolbe who swam three miles up a river after failing to save a drowning Australian in 1900; and two Cape Town society marriages of 1890. NONE OF THEM CONNECTS TO ANYTHING HERE and none is being adopted because the surname is rare enough to tempt.
no

sets.g: The seven Marico claims read to the bottom — and a farm school nobody had asked for
sets.n: The index line was the whole record; the same query returned forty-eight files about a school
rows: NOTHING BEYOND THE INITIALS

Every one of the seven reads, in full: “CLAIMS FOR COMPENSATION BURGHERS. MARICO. XX BOOYZEN.” No remarks field, no farm, no forename, no amount. THE INDEX LINE IS THE WHOLE RECORD. This archive has spent two days treating these seven as a lead that could be worked at a screen. They cannot. Moved to the errands page, which is where a thing belongs when the only remaining step is a door.
no
BOOYZEN AND MARICO, Transvaal depot
TEN DOCUMENTS — SEVEN CLAIMS AND THREE NOBODY HAD ASKED FOR

The other three are TAB source OD, the education files of the South African Republic, and all three are about a school: a subsidy application, a book order and a set of quarterly returns, each headed “H DE VRIES, JGL BOOYZEN, KWAGGAFONTEIN, DISTRIK MARICO, PK KAFFERSKRAAL”. The first carries a remarks field pointing at an earlier file, OR13059/97. THE REMARKS FIELD IS THE THREAD.
yes
Pull the thread — KWAGGAFONTEIN in the Transvaal depot
72 DOCUMENTS; 48 OF THEM THIS SCHOOL

From 4 October 1897, when G.E. ter Haar of Kafferskraal asked the government for a teacher, to April 1900, when the teacher asked for his cheque to be sent to the landdrost and the war ended the file. In between: the school commission finds a teacher (N. de Vries); a telegram — “wagon leaves Thursday to fetch teacher De Vries, is everything in order?”; inspection reports by inspector T.C. Stoffberg; a dispute over when the teacher moved into his house; a subsidy chased; school furniture bought; holidays; and two pupils leaving.
yes
Which of the forty-eight carry the surname
EIGHT, AND ALWAYS IN THE SAME PLACE

JGL Booyzen is named on the subsidy application, two book orders, all four quarterly returns, the explanation of an adverse balance of £61-6-0, and a letter of May 1899 telling the department that IN HIS OPINION £8 TOO LITTLE SUBSIDY HAD BEEN PAID, with reasons. He is on none of the holiday notices, form requests or railway certificates, which the teacher sent alone. THAT IS THE SHAPE OF A SCHOOL COMMISSION'S TREASURER, not a teacher and not a parent.
yes
Which JGL Booyzen
NOT ANSWERED, AND NOT GUESSED

The elder Jan Gerthardus Lodewikus, born about 1818, DIED AT VAALBANK ON 25 MAY 1885 and cannot be this man. His namesake born 4 December 1855 would be forty-two in 1898 and is a man of whom this archive has said for months that nothing is known of what became of him. Marico adjoins Lichtenburg; this family is documented in Marico from 1892. IT IS ALSO ONE OF THE COMMONEST NAME-STRINGS IN THE SURNAME. Recorded open.
part
The spelling, in one office, over ten months
BOOYZEN, BOOYSEN, BOOIJZEN — THE SAME MAN

January 1898 BOOYZEN; 12 February BOOYSEN; 9 May BOOYSEN; 1 July BOOYZEN; 20 October BOOIJZEN; 15 December BOOYSEN. One man, one farm, one government department, one register series, one year. NOTHING IN THIS ARCHIVE HAS SHOWN THE POINT SO CLEANLY: the z is not a branch and the ij is not a generation, it is whichever clerk had the pen.
yes
BOOYSEN AND ONDERWYZER, Transvaal depot
SIXTEEN — AND ONE OF THEM IS ON THIS FAMILY'S OWN FARM

Most are other Booysens running other farm schools across the republic: Wonderboom, Hartsenbergfontein, Kareeboomputten, Zeekoefontein. But OR19199/98 and OR19484/98 read “DS. BOOYSEN (ONDERWYZER JP LOUW) VAALBANK DISTRICT LICHTENBURG POSTMERK RIETKUIL” — VAALBANK IS THE FARM WHERE JAN GERTHARDUS LODEWIKUS BOOIJSEN DIED IN 1885 AND HIS DAUGHTER IN 1920. He sends the school's power of attorney and eighteen pence in stamps to the government bookkeeper, and co-signs the fourth-quarter returns.
yes
And the best of the three Vaalbank files
OR2037/99, 6 FEBRUARY 1899 — SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ORPHANS

“DS. BOOIJSEN, LOUW (ONDERWIJZER), VAALBANK, DISTRIK LICHTENBURG, PK RIETKUIL. VRAAGT INLICHTINGEN OVER HET VERSCHAFFEN VAN LEERMIDDELEN AAN WEEZEN, NAAR AANLEIDING VAN EEN GEVAL TEN HUNNEN.” Asks how school materials may be provided to orphans, arising from a case among them. It is the only document in this archive in which a Booysen writes to a government about a child who is not his own.
yes
Is DS. a pair of initials or the Dutch Ds. for dominee
CANNOT BE READ FROM AN INDEX LINE

David Schalk is this family's most used name-string, and DS. on this farm in 1898 would put a named relative on it. BUT SIX WEEKS EARLIER THE SAME SCHOOL WROTE “JP LOUW DS VAN ROOJEN” IN EXACTLY THE SAME SLOT, and Ds. van Rooijen is far more likely a minister. One abbreviation, two readings, and this archive will not choose between them to make the better story true. The file settles it in a sentence; it has gone on the errands page.
part
The atlas line that said “in the field-cornet's papers”
WRONG, AND CORRECTED IN PLACE

The papers are the education department's. A field-cornet appears in the bundle exactly once, valuing the teacher's dwelling in May 1898, in a document sent by somebody else. The line had been written from a memory of the record rather than from the record, and it survived because nothing on the site cited it. AN EVENT WITH NO CITATION IS AN EVENT NOBODY CAN CHECK.
yes

sets.g: Nine places put on the atlas — items 4 and 6
sets.n: 54 places become 63, and two farms are pinned on inferences that are labelled
rows: The seven towns, which needed no argument
PHILIPPOLIS · BETHULIE · UITENHAGE · PIET RETIEF · HOOPSTAD · STEYNSBURG · QUEENSTOWN

All seven came out of two days' work and none was on the map. PHILIPPOLIS is where the 1868 obituary says the Settler's children grew up — a fourth independent source for what this archive had inferred from baptism places. BETHULIE is where FREDERIK FORTUNATUS was born in 1839 and where he brought his own youngest daughter to be baptised FORTY-TWO YEARS LATER. UITENHAGE is where the eldest son was born in 1822, two years after the landing.
yes
LEEUWBERG, where the Commandant died
PINNED AT FAURESMITH, ON ONE LAND FILE

A Free State land file of 1903 reads “LEEUWBERG NO 465 DIST. FAURISMITH EXTENT ABOUT 1 200 MORGEN”. That is a farm of the right name in the right province THIRTY-FIVE YEARS AFTER HE DIED THERE, and nothing more. Farm names repeat. THE PIN CARRIES THE CAVEAT ON THE MAP.
part
KAALSPRUIT, where he lived and lies
PINNED AT BLOEMFONTEIN, ON A PAIR OF NAMES

His own advertisement of 9 March 1864 is signed from “Kafferberg, Kaalspruit”. A Free State soil-conservation district is registered as “KAALSPRUIT – KAFFERRIVIER (BLOEMFONTEIN)” — THE SAME TWO NAMES PAIRED, in the district whose bank he directed and whose paper he advertised in. A NAME PAIR IS NOT A SURVEY BEACON and the pin says so.
part
The part that does not fit, said out loud
FAURESMITH AND BLOEMFONTEIN ARE 130 KILOMETRES APART

The obituary says he died at LEEUWBERG and that he “settled on the farm where he died and now lies buried on KAALSPRUIT”. Those cannot both be true of two farms that far apart. EITHER ONE OF THIS ARCHIVE'S TWO IDENTIFICATIONS IS WRONG, OR THE OBITUARY IS LOOSE. Both pins are marked approximate and the contradiction is printed with them rather than smoothed over by choosing one.
part

sets.g: The Friend of the Free State — the paper that printed the obituary first
sets.n: Eight sons and four daughters, a farm settled, and a sister's death dated
rows: The Friend, 10 April 1868 — five days before the Grahamstown Journal
THE GRAHAMSTOWN VERSION IS A REPRINT, AND IT DROPS A LINE

The Friend is the Free State paper and printed it first. Its wording: “OF THE EIGHT SONS AND FOUR DAUGHTERS HE HAS LEFT BEHIND HIM, one daughter alone is married, the youngest being but an infant.” THE GRAHAMSTOWN REPRINT SAYS ONLY “OF FOUR DAUGHTERS”. So the twelve children are EIGHT SONS AND FOUR DAUGHTERS, which this archive did not know an hour ago. The transcriber also notes that the obituary “continues for a further half column, but is very difficult to read” — SO THERE IS MORE, AND IT IS NOT TRANSCRIBED.
yes
Two transcriptions of one sentence, disagreeing on the farm
KAALSPRUIT AGAINST “[RANDSPRUIT]”

Grahamstown: “settled on the farm where he died and now lies on KAALSPRUIT”. The Friend: “now lies buried on [RANDSPRUIT]”, the brackets the transcriber's own admission of doubt. ONE OF THE TWO IS WRONG AND THIS ARCHIVE COULD NOT SAY WHICH.
part
And the man settles it himself, four years earlier
“J.G.E. KOLBE, Kafferberg, KAALSPRUIT, 9 March 1864”

A lost-property advertisement in the Friend, signed with his own address as the paper printed it. KAALSPRUIT IS RIGHT AND THE BRACKETED READING IS WRONG. The advertisement does a second job: it concerns “a promissory note, date 9th March 1864, DRAWN BY GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE IN FAVOR OF J.G.E. KOLBE, payable 4 months after date for £154 Stg”, lost on the Market Square at Bloemfontein. THE SETTLER'S ELDEST SON AND HIS TWIN-BORN BROTHER, IN ONE DOCUMENT, OVER A DEBT.
yes
The Friend, 23 October 1863 — an estate notice, printed twice
A SISTER'S DEATH, DATED AT LAST

“Derwyl MARIA ELIZABETH KOLBE zonder testament na te laten is overleden en de nagebleven echtgenoot G.F. ENSLIN … als executeur is aangesteld.” MARY ELIZABETH KOLBE DIED INTESTATE and her husband George Frederick Enslin was appointed executor of her estate. This archive had “bef. 1867”, inferred from a baptism. IT IS NOW BEFORE 23 OCTOBER 1863, from a notice her own husband placed in the paper.
yes
A note on how the address is printed here
AS THE PAPER PRINTED IT, AND NOT USED AS A LABEL

The 1864 advertisement gives his address with a place-name that is a racial slur in South African English. This archive quotes the advertisement as it stands, because that is what quoting a document means, and does not carry the word anywhere else — the farm is indexed as KAALSPRUIT.
part

sets.g: Margaret Downing — item 11, answered by a photograph already in this archive
sets.n: The Burgersdorp monument, read to the end
rows: NAAIRS · KOLBE AND DOWNING
SIXTEEN DOCUMENTS, AND NO DEATH NOTICE FOR HER

A WILL OF HER OWN, MOOC 7/1/295 no. 70, made in 1854 — ten years after she was widowed. Her husband's 1844 WILL, 1845 INVENTORY and 1845 APPRAISEMENT, MOOC 7/1/180 nos. 52–54. 1841 England census, HO107, piece 734, book 1, folio 11, page 15, SCHEDULE 38 — St George Hanover Square, sub-district MAY FAIR, street CONDUIT STREET. “JOHN G KOLBE, male, age 76, birth year 1765, birth county as transcribed: FOREIGN.” Two things follow. “Unfortunately the Background File does not give any further information on the donation or any other donations by Dr. Griffiths.” The whereabouts of the original is not recorded and cannot be pursued from that end. A CLEAN NEGATIVE FROM THE ONLY PLACE THAT COULD HAVE ANSWERED IT.

“kind love from your Sisters & brother”
THE LINE THAT DATES THE OBITUARY

SISTERS PLURAL, BROTHER SINGULAR, August 1830. Of the EIGHT SONS the 1844 obituary counts, EXACTLY TWO WERE ALIVE — George Augustus at the Cape and Henry in London with dropsy. Henry, from his father's pen
DROPSY, AND “RESIGNED TO THE CATASTROPHE”

Melanie Geustyn, Senior Librarian, National Library of South Africa, with the Background File in front of her: “The author, KS, WOULD BE DR. “Unfortunately the Background File does not give any further information on the donation or any other donations by Dr. Griffiths.” A librarian went to the off-site vaults, pulled the accession file and looked. The 1802 birth; J.G.E. Kolbe 1822–68 at Leeuberg as a commandant; Margaret Downing 1803–1867; the 1819 London marriage at a very young age; the apothecary’s trade on the settler roll; the farm Wurthemberg; ten children; Philippolis from March 1831 (this archive has a daughter born there that year). Is the entry right that the Settler’s father was a German apothecary?
NO — HE WAS A TAILOR, AND THE ARCHIVE CAN PROVE IT SEVEN WAYS

121 Westminster rate book entries, the printed roll of 234 master tailors of 1799, the master tailors’ list of April 1834, three London Gazette dissolutions all reading TAILORS, the 1841 census occupation column, the Westminster burial register, and John Henry Kolbe’s deposition on oath at the Old Bailey in 1819. THE TRADE IS THE SON’S, MOVED ONE GENERATION UP. The entry is accurate wherever its author had a record; the one thing he had no record for is the one thing he got wrong.

Does the entry’s “Knapdaar” contradict the obituary’s “Wirtemberg”?

“die plaas Wurthemberg (soms ook aangegee as Knapdaar)”. The heading alone looked like a conflict and the body resolves it. What this archive gains is A SECOND NAME TO SEARCH in the deeds records and NAAIRS.

Was MSB 751 written “on his ordination”, as the catalogue says?
NO — THE ORDINATION WAS 25 MAY 1833

Two years and nine months after the letter. The letter reports acceptance as a missionary, which is a different step, and the entry supplies a third — mission assistant on 8 February 1828. THE ARCHIVE HAD REPEATED A FINDING AID AS THOUGH IT WERE THE DOCUMENT. Logged as a correction.

“Extract from the journal of Messrs Melvill and Kolbe”, Transactions of the Missionary Society (1829) — is it online?

THE PRINTED VERSION IS FILED UNDER THE OTHER MAN’S NAME. Full citation: “Extracts of the Journal of Messrs Melvill and Kolbe, ADDRESSED TO THE REV. RICHARD MILES, Superintendent of the Society’s Missions in Africa, Philippolis, 25 NOV. 1828”, Council for World Missions (LMS) Archives — WHICH IS SOURCE 4 ON THE DSAB’S OWN LIST, two lines above source 6, and the entry never says they are the same document. “An edited version, dated 18 Nov. 1828, appears in MELVILL (1829).” Legassick quotes it: the travellers met refugee groups with “no other means of subsistence than the wild animals found in these parts” — THE FIRST WORDS OF GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE’S THIS ARCHIVE HAS READ, and they are about famine. AND THE JOURNEY IS PRINTED IN FULL IN A BOOK STILL SOLD: Karel Schoeman (ed.), Early White Travellers in the Transgariep, 1819–1840 (Protea Book House, 2003), p. 30. The Google Books API refuses this archive entirely — HTTP 429 to every query — and the same searches through the ordinary Books interface returned all of this in four minutes.

Sibree, A register of missionaries, 4th ed. (LMS, 1923) — is it online?
NOT FOUND under that title on the Internet Archive
It would give his LMS service dates in a single printed line, which is exactly what is wanted to test 8 February 1828, 25 May 1833 and 19 June 1837. Searched, not found, and left on the work list.

Is there any published corroboration of the Bethanie claim of 1834, independent of this entry?
NO — IT LOOKED LIKE TWO WITNESSES AND IT IS ONE

An encyclopaedia article states that the Berlin Missionary Society founded Bethanien for the Korana in September 1834 on the advice of the LMS’s G.A. Kolbe at Philippolis — AND ITS FOOTNOTE CITES SCHOEMAN’S OWN 1985 BOOK, Die Huis van die Armes. THE DRAFT ENTRY AND THE ARTICLE REST ON THE SAME MAN’S RESEARCH. This archive nearly published it as independent corroboration and it is not. A claim repeated in two places can still be a single witness.

Are the Griqua Council’s own papers for 1836 in print?
YES — AND THE ENTRY COULD NOT CITE THEM

Karel Schoeman (ed.), Griqua Records: the Philippolis Captaincy, 1825–1861, Van Riebeeck Society II/25 — 162 official and semi-official documents including the Philippolis Law Book and the correspondence between the Captaincy’s officials and the missionaries. PUBLISHED TWO YEARS AFTER THIS TYPESCRIPT WAS TYPED. It is the obvious place to test the 1836 accusation, the Hendricks agitation and the acquittal. Available as a purchasable eBook from HIPSA; no free digitisation found.
yes
Is a portrait of George Augustus Kolbe known to exist?
THE ENTRY NAMES TWO

A likeness of him AS A YOUNG MAN, in 1992 with C.J. du Plessis of Ruigtevlei, district Bethulie, reproduced in Burger Olivier’s So onthou ons die oewerbewoners van ou “Grootrivier” (1973); and a CHARLES BELL WATERCOLOUR OF A CHURCH SERVICE AT PHILIPPOLIS IN 1834 WITH KOLBE IN THE PULPIT, in the Africana Museum, Johannesburg, reproduced in The Journal of Andrew Smith, ed. Lye (1975). THIS ARCHIVE HOLDS NO LIKENESS OF ANYBODY BORN BEFORE 1850. Neither has been seen.
yes
Can the Charles Bell picture of Kolbe be found?
YES — AND IN A COUNTRY THE ENTRY DOES NOT MENTION

University of Edinburgh, Centre for the Study of World Christianity, **CSWC 60** — five photographs, 1834–1840, photograph copies of sketches by C. Bell of African congregations. ITEM 3 IS “MR. KOLBE… AT PHILIPPOLIS IN 1834”. The DSAB sends the reader to the Africana Museum in Johannesburg for the original watercolour and says nothing of Scotland; Edinburgh’s catalogue says nothing of Johannesburg. The other four sitters include JEAN-PIERRE PELLISSIER, who is source 9 on the DSAB’s own list.
yes
Does Edinburgh describe him correctly?
NO — IT CALLS HIM “A MORAVIAN MISSIONARY?”

With the question mark. He was LONDON MISSIONARY SOCIETY, on the NLSA’s catalogue of MSB 751 and on his own father’s letter of 23 August 1830 — “fully accepted by the [L.M.S.] as one of their Missionaries”. THIS IS THE FIRST TIME THIS ARCHIVE HAS BEEN IN A POSITION TO CORRECT AN INSTITUTION RATHER THAN BE CORRECTED BY ONE, and the letter that does it can ask for a copy of the photograph at the same time.

Is the “Mr Miles” of the 1830 letter the Richard Miles of the 1828 journal?
VERY PROBABLY — AND IT IS AN INFERENCE, NOT A DOCUMENT

Richard Miles, formerly pastor of Brigg in Lincolnshire and appointed to Demerara, was sent to Cape Town TO ACT AS DR PHILIP’S SUBSTITUTE WHILE PHILIP WAS IN ENGLAND. Philip was in England from 1826; Miles was acting Superintendent at the Cape in 1828, which is why Kolbe addressed his journal to him there; by 1830 Philip was back and Miles was in London, calling at a tailor’s house in Soho. THE LETTER SAYS ONLY “MR MILES” AND GIVES NO FORENAME, so the office, the continent and the dates carry it and nothing else does. Published as an inference and marked as one.

sets.g: MSB 751 read again, from the file rather than from a preview
sets.n: the same four pages at full resolution, two days later — nothing wrong, a good deal missing
rows: Does the full-resolution reading contradict anything already published?
NO — NOT ONE WORD

The heading “London August 23. 1830”, the opening “Dear George”, the L.M.S. acceptance, Mr Miles calling at the house, Dr Philip carrying the earlier letter, HENRY AND THE DROPSY AND “RESIGNED TO THE CATASTROPHE”, Milne and Betsey removed to EDINBURGH, Charlotte’s Evangelical Magazine, the suit of black clothes, George IV and William IV, the French revolution of July 1830, and — the line the whole argument rests on — “KIND LOVE FROM YOUR SISTERS & BROTHER”. ALL CONFIRMED FROM THE FILE.
yes
Was Dr Philip only the courier?
NO — HE IS IN THE ROOM, AND HE IS PLEASED

“Dr Philip was exceedingly glad to hear of you being accepted by the L.M.S. as you may well imagine, HE HAS PROMISED TO WRITE TO YOU A LETTER BY THE FIRST OPPORTUNITY.” This archive had him as a man carrying an envelope. HE IS IN LONDON IN AUGUST 1830, he has heard the news, and he undertakes to write to George himself. THAT LETTER, IF IT WAS WRITTEN, IS ANOTHER DOCUMENT WITH GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE’S NAME ON IT, and the place to look is the CWM archive at SOAS that holds his journal.
yes
Who is the “John” the clothes are for?
VERY PROBABLY THE COMMANDANT, AGED EIGHT

“I have enclosed also a Jacket & waistcoat for John & a further Jacket also for him, tell him HIS OLD FATHER has sent it him, & TO MAKE HASTE TO FILL THEM OUT.” Clothes for a growing child. George Augustus’s eldest son was JOHN GERSON ELIEZAR KOLBE, BORN 7 JULY 1822 — eight years old in August 1830, and the man who died a commandant at Leeuwberg in 1868. IF THAT IS HIM, THIS IS THE EARLIEST DOCUMENT IN THIS ARCHIVE THAT MENTIONS HIM. “His old father” is the difficulty and is not glossed over: the writer is the boy’s GRANDFATHER. Marked as an inference.
part
Does the letter name anybody outside the family?
YES — FIVE PEOPLE, AND NONE OF THEM IS ANYWHERE ELSE HERE

Mr & Mrs STANHOPE; Mr WARNER and Mrs WARNER; MRS FIELD AND HER DAUGHTERS, of whom “the eldest, Miss Mary, that was, HAS MARRIED A MR BELLEW, A SURGEON, whom I do not know whether you may recollect”. This archive has had the Soho household entirely through official paper — rate books, a census, the Gazette, a burial register. THESE ARE THE FIRST PEOPLE IN IT WHO SIMPLY KNEW THEM. A surgeon named Bellew marrying a Miss Mary Field about 1829–30 is searchable.
yes
What is the story from The Mirror that he asks his son to check?
TWO PAGES, AND THE STRANGEST THING IN THE LETTER

A Scottish colonist, “either Williams, or Williamson”, settled close to the Xhosa; orang-outangs raid his fruit; he shoots a young one that proves to be a chief’s son; weeks later MRS W. IS CARRIED OFF; he suspects a Xhosa chief who had offered oxen and “2 or 3 of his finest caffre women” for her and been refused, whose messenger had said “YOU WILL REPENT OF YOUR OBSTINACY”; he raises a company of soldiers under CAPT JOHNSON and is on the point of war when a witness is produced who saw an orang-outang carrying a woman across the river; the chief then furnishes his own men to help, and after nearly two years she is found living among the animals AS THEIR QUEEN. THE FATHER DOES NOT BELIEVE IT — “here we look upon the Story as a fictious & romance” — and writes to the one man he knows who is actually there to ask “whether that report may be founded in truth, or falsehood”. THE NUMBER OF THE MIRROR HAS NOT BEEN FOUND.
part
Do the margins give the street address after all?
NO — AND THEY ARE THE ONLY LINES NOT READ

Pages two and four carry notes written across the fold about HOW TO DIRECT THE BOX, naming the Revd MR MURRAY and DR PHILIP. They are partly illegible at this resolution and are NOT GUESSED AT. Everything else in four pages has been read. Brunswick Square against Conduit Street remains open.

rows: Is Sibree’s Register (LMS, 1923) online?
YES — FREE, 225 PAGES, AND THIS ARCHIVE SAID IT WAS NOT

A complete PDF at missiology.org.uk. This archive searched the INTERNET ARCHIVE, found nothing under that title, and published “not found”. THAT WAS A NEGATIVE ABOUT ONE SHELF REPORTED AS A NEGATIVE ABOUT THE WORLD — the same fault this archive names on /method/ as the reason a nil return is worthless without a control. The Google Books API refuses this machine outright (HTTP 429 to every query); the ordinary web search found it in one attempt.
yes
Does it hold George Augustus Kolbe?
YES — ENTRY 278, AND IT IS HIS WHOLE MISSION LIFE

“Was previously connected with the GRAAFF REINET MISSIONARY SOCIETY, and laboured AMONG THE SLAVES around Graaff Reinet. Was accepted provisionally by MR. MILES, FEB. 8, 1829, which action was confirmed by the Directors, JULY 29, 1829. First laboured with MR. CLARK, at the BUSHMAN STATION, CALEDON RIVER. Thence proceeded to PHILIPPOLIS, arriving there, MARCH 13, 1831. On MAY 26, 1833, he was ordained by the French missionaries, Messrs. LEMUE, PELLISIER, AND ARBOUSSET. His connection was dissolved by the Directors, JUNE 19, 1837.” Index: service 1829–1837.
yes
Who was the “Mr Miles” who called at the tailor’s house in 1830?
THE MAN WHO ACCEPTED HIM — NOT A MESSENGER

“Accepted PROVISIONALLY BY MR. MILES, Feb. 8, 1829, which action was CONFIRMED BY THE DIRECTORS, July 29, 1829.” Richard Miles was Acting Superintendent of the LMS at Cape Town from 1825, sent to stand in for Dr Philip while Philip was in Britain. AND IT EXPLAINS THE FATHER’S ADVERB: provisionally by Miles, confirmed by the Directors, and a father told his son had been “FULLY accepted”. The letter is using the Society’s own vocabulary correctly, because the officer concerned was in the room.
yes
Does Sibree agree with the DSAB draft?
ON THREE POINTS EXACTLY, AND NOT ON THREE OTHERS

AGREE: the Graaff-Reinet society and the slaves, almost word for word; Clark and the Bushman station; the dissolution on 19 June 1837 to the day. DIFFER: acceptance 8 February 1829, not 1828; Philippolis 13 March 1831, which is finer than Schoeman’s “March 1831” and agrees with it; ordination 26 MAY 1833 not the 25th, and by LEMUE, PELLISSIER AND ARBOUSSET — three men, WITH NO CASALIS. Pellissier is source 9 on Schoeman’s own list. BOTH ARE PRINTED WORKS AND NEITHER IS THE MANUSCRIPT; this archive gives both and prefers neither in print.
part
Was F.W. Kolbe of the Rhenish Mission related to this family?
NO — AND THE LMS’S OWN REGISTER IS THE ONE THAT IS WRONG

Sibree, entry 522: “KOLBE, Frederick William. Born, Nov. 3, 1821, in South Africa. SON OF REV. G. A. KOLBE (No. 278).” Died at Cape Town 25 December 1899 aged 78; author of an English–Herero Dictionary. Schoeman: “F.W. Kolbe (1821–99) van die Rynse Sendinggenootskap was NIE aan hierdie familie verwant nie.” SAME MAN, SAME SOCIETY, SAME YEARS. AND HE CANNOT BE ADOPTED ON SIBREE’S WORD: 3 November 1821 agrees with his age at death, and the Settler’s known eldest was born 7 JULY 1822, which agrees with HIS age at death. EIGHT MONTHS APART. Sibree also gives a sister, CHARLOTTE KOLBE born 25 December 1829, who married Rev. William Sykes at Paarl in 1860. NOT ADOPTED, NOT DISMISSED, AND ON THE WORK LIST. RESOLVED THE SAME AFTERNOON. THREE INDEPENDENT WORKS AGAINST SIBREE: the New Catholic Encyclopedia on his son Monsignor F.C. Kolbe — “the son of a WESTPHALIAN (GERMAN) PROTESTANT MISSIONARY who had married the daughter of a member of the London Missionary Society”; S2A3, which names him FRIEDRICH WILHELM KOLBE, Rhenish missionary and Herero scholar, married at Cape Town in 1849 and at Okahandja by April 1850; and DSAB VOL. 5 (1987), which has its own entry on him and was in print five years before Schoeman wrote, which is why the draft marks him with an asterisk. SIBREE HAS TWO KOLBES IN SOUTH AFRICA, ENTRIES 278 AND 522, AND A COMPILER JOINED THEM. Charlotte Kolbe born 25 December 1829 goes with him.

sets.g: The Nautilus roll, and the story from The Mirror
sets.n: two more of Schoeman’s eleven sources worked — one delivered, one did not
rows: What does the settler roll actually say?
“KOLBE, GEORGE AUGUSTUS 20. CHEMIST. W MARGARET 19.”

From Nash’s Settler Handbook, page 98, published in full at 1820settlers.com. HE WAS SIXTEEN — born 7 December 1802 and sailing from Gravesend on 3 December 1819, four days before his seventeenth birthday. SHE WAS SIXTEEN. About three years added to each.
yes
Is the roll consistent with the marriage allegation?
NO — AND THAT IS THE INTERESTING PART

At Shoreditch on 20 January 1819 both swore to being “of the age of Twenty-one Years and upwards”, because a minor could not marry by licence without a parent’s consent. ELEVEN MONTHS LATER HE IS TWENTY AND SHE IS NINETEEN. Nobody twenty-one and upwards in January is twenty in December. THEY WERE NOT MAINTAINING A FICTION; THEY WERE TELLING EACH DOCUMENT WHAT IT NEEDED.
yes
What became of Owen’s party?
IT COLLAPSED IN 1821, AND IT EXPLAINS THE GAP

Fifty-two people, No. 3 on the Colonial Department list, joint-stock and recruited in London by THOMAS OWEN OF 9 CAREY STREET, HORSEFERRY ROAD, WESTMINSTER, correspondence handled by his father the REV J OWEN OF FULHAM. Located at SPANISH REED PLACE near the Kap River. Owen — “this querulous man”, per Special Commissioner Hayward — REFUSED TO DRAW RATIONS FOR HIS PEOPLE; his brother W.S. Owen replaced him; Owen left early in 1821 and the party dispersed. THE SETTLER WAS EIGHTEEN, WITH NO LEADER, NO RATIONS AND NO LOCATION, and the next record of him is the Graaff-Reinet mission about three years later.
yes
Is there an original roll to go back to?
THREE CAPE ARCHIVES REFERENCES, AND NO SHIP’S RETURN

CO 6137/1,4 (the list under Owen’s direction), CO 8543 (Hayward’s notes) and CO 3917 (THE MEMORIAL OF INDEPENDENT SETTLERS ABOARD THE NAUTILUS). A MEMORIAL IS A PETITION AND A PETITION IS SIGNED — that one could carry his signature at seventeen. Nash records that NO AGENT OF TRANSPORTS’ RETURN HAS EVER BEEN TRACED for the Nautilus, so these three are the whole basis of the roll.
yes
Can the story from The Mirror be found?
NO — SEARCHED AND NOT FOUND

Two of the father’s four pages go on it and he asks his son to say whether it is true. Searched Google Books and the open web on the story’s own terms — “ourang outang” and “orang outang” with carried off, wife, colonist, Caffre, Mirror, 1829 and 1830 — AND GOOGLE BOOKS RETURNED NO MATCHES AT ALL. Recorded so nobody repeats these terms. NEXT: the runs of The Mirror on Project Gutenberg and the Internet Archive, searched volume by volume rather than by phrase, and the names WILLIAMS or WILLIAMSON with CAPT JOHNSON.

rows: Does SOAS hold anything in George Augustus Kolbe’s own hand?
FOUR JOURNALS, 1828 TO 1834

CWM/LMS/05/05/100 — “Extracts from the Journal of JOHN MELVILL AND GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE, during a tour to the north-eastwards of Philippolis, 13–22 NOV 1828”, which is THE MANUSCRIPT BEHIND SOURCE 6 and carries the days of the journey. /102 — extracts, Philippolis, 1828–1831. /106 — Journal, Philippolis, 1831–1834. /108 — Journal, Philippolis, 6 Oct 1832 – Sep 1833. UNTIL THIS AFTERNOON THE SUM OF HIS OWN WORDS IN THIS ARCHIVE WAS ONE SENTENCE QUOTED AT SECOND HAND.
yes
Is the correspondence for the year of the accusation identifiable?
YES — AND IT IS A SINGLE BOX

CWM/LMS/05/02/02/044, South Africa 1835, WHICH THE CATALOGUE SAYS CONTAINS “GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE, PHILIPPOLIS” among its correspondents; /046, South Africa 1836; and the 1837 file. The sub-series note gives the boxes: 1835 is Box 14B and 1836–1837 IS BOX 15. The accusation and the dismissal are in one box, and this archive has been repeating a one-sentence summary of them.
yes
Is there a portrait of a Kolbe at SOAS?
YES — AND IT IS THE WRONG KOLBE

CWM/LMS/01/09/02/01/525, Missionary Portraits — “SYKES, CHARLOTTE NÉE KOLBE (S. Africa 1858–1887)”. She is the sister of the Rhenish missionary Friedrich Wilhelm Kolbe, whom the same afternoon’s work placed outside this family. RECORDED SO THAT NOBODY HERE MAKES SIBREE’S MISTAKE IN THE OTHER DIRECTION.

Does the archive corroborate the F.W. Kolbe resolution?
YES — FROM A FOURTH DIRECTION

Reports by Frederick Kolbe from PAARL in 1867, 1868, 1870, 1871, 1872, 1873 and 1875 and from STELLENBOSCH in 1876; incoming letters from GEORGE in 1854, Paarl from 1858 and Cape Town to 1899; and in the 1893 file, “Frederick Kolbe, Cape Town — DEATH OF MRS KOLBE [NÉE ISABELLA MARIA ELLIOTT]”. That is the S2A3 entry matched to the person, in the Society’s own files.

sets.g: A Geni profile for the Commandant’s son — tested, not adopted
sets.n: a stranger’s tree, checked against documents this archive reached by another road
rows: Is this the same circular trap as the MyHeritage result?
NO — AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE WHOLE POINT

The earlier search returned THIS FAMILY’S OWN TREE handed back through MyHeritage, which corroborates nothing. THE COMMANDANT’S TWELVE CHILDREN HAVE NEVER BEEN IN THIS ARCHIVE AT ALL — his 1868 obituary counts them and names none, and a work-list row has stood for a fortnight asking for the estate that would name them. A collaborative tree naming them is INDEPENDENT of anything here.
yes
Does it agree with anything this archive can check?
TWICE, AND NEITHER IS A COINCIDENCE THE COMPILERS COULD HAVE ENGINEERED

One: the profile gives his wife as MARIA PETRONELLA ELIZABETH ANTOINETTE and his daughter as ROSA MAGDALENE — and this archive holds, from the BLOEMFONTEIN BAPTISM REGISTER, a ROSA MAGDALENA KOLBE baptised 1890 to Frederik Fortuna Kolbe and MARIA PETRONELLA ELIZABETH ANTOINETTA McCABE. Two: it lists MARIA MARGARETHA DOWNING ROUSSEAU as his daughter, and this archive holds TAB MHG 5450/68 under exactly that name — AN ORPHAN INDEX ENTRY THAT NOW HAS A FATHER.
yes
Is it therefore evidence?
NO, AND TWELVE PEOPLE ARE NOT BEING ENTERED ON IT

One source attached, four profile managers, added in 2014. IT IS A LIST WORTH WORKING, WHICH IS WHAT SCHOEMAN’S BIBLIOGRAPHY WAS. The difference between a tree and a source is not that one is always wrong — it is that ONE HAS TO BE TESTED AND THE OTHER HAS ALREADY BEEN. The document that tests it is VAB MHG M777 at Bloemfontein, already on the work list, and it is now a better thing to order because there is something to check it against.
part
Does it settle the Kolbe–McCabe question this archive raised?
IT OFFERS AN ANSWER, AND IT IS THE OBVIOUS ONE

The Commandant’s widow ANNA JACOBA VAN DER MERWE married FRANCIS McCABE, Landdrost of Bloemfontein, about April 1871; McCabe died in February 1872 leaving “four sons and two daughters, BESIDES A LARGE FAMILY OF STEP-CHILDREN”. Her son then married a McCABE. THE TWO HOUSEHOLDS WERE ONE FOR ELEVEN MONTHS. This archive called it a possible coincidence; on this reading it is a stepfamily marrying within itself, which is ordinary. NOT PROVED — the marriage record would prove it.
part
Is this Frederik Fortunatus one of the men this archive already holds?
NO — HE IS A FOURTH OF THE NAME

Every FamilySearch citation on this site is a RECORD — an indexed register entry with an ark. Does the FamilySearch tree match documents held here?
THREE MORE TIMES

ANNA JACOBA VAN DER MERWE 1824–1896 against VAB MHG M777, her 1896 estate. Where does it lose?
MARY LARMAN, AND NOT NARROWLY

sets.g: FindMyPast swept for a Downing–Pooley marriage
sets.n: a name off a user tree, taken to the index the same afternoon
rows: Is there a Downing–Pooley marriage before civil registration?
YES — EXACTLY ONE, AND IT IS IN DEVON

JOHN DOWNING married MARY POOLEY, 10 MAY 1802, WELCOMBE (BISHOP’S TRANSCRIPTS), DEVON, Anglican — Devon Marriages and Banns, GBPRS/M/514168016/1, transcribed by the Devon Family History Society. Against 231,425 Downing records and 65,460 Pooley records in the Life Events collection, TWELVE match the pair at all, of which three are indexed marriages and the other two are 1882 and 1955. THE DATE IS NINE MONTHS AND THIRTEEN DAYS BEFORE MARGARET DOWNING’S BIRTH ON 23 FEBRUARY 1803.
yes
Does the county fit?
YES, AND FROM A DIRECTION THAT KNEW NOTHING ABOUT IT

This archive’s own family tree puts the Downings in DEVON — Edward Downing m. Mary HEARD, Thomas Downing m. Mary TRICK, John Trick m. Margaret HOOPER. Trick, Heard and Hooper are Devon names and WELCOMBE IS A NORTH DEVON PARISH ON THE CORNISH BORDER. The tree and the register agree about the county independently.
yes
Can it be tied to Margaret Downing?
NO — AND THE DOCUMENT THAT WOULD DO IT IS NOT THERE

SHE WAS BORN IN LONDON. A couple married in a remote North Devon parish with a child in London nine months later is possible and is not shown. NO BAPTISM FOR MARGARET DOWNING IN LONDON IN 1803 WAS FOUND — the collection was searched by name and year and returns nothing of the kind. A baptism naming both parents is what would settle it. THIS IS A CANDIDATE AND NOT A FINDING.
part
Was the name that launched the search even right?
THE TWO TREES DO NOT AGREE

The FamilySearch Family Tree calls her MARY KING POOLEY. The family tree this archive was built from calls her MARY P KING — SURNAME KING, WITH AN INITIAL. So the “P” may be Pooley, or “Pooley” may be somebody’s later reading of the “P”. THE SEARCH MAY HAVE BEEN LOOKING FOR A SURNAME THAT IS NOT HERS. They differ on her husband too: John Paul Downing is 1769–1839 in one and 1765–1839 in the other. HER OWN DEATH NOTICE, THE ONLY DOCUMENT EVER ASKED, SAYS “BOTH DEAD” AND NAMES NEITHER PARENT.

Does the FindMyPast `Keywords` filter actually filter?
YES — TESTED WITH A NONSENSE VALUE

The driver notes record that KeywordsPlace and YearOfBirth are SCORED and do not restrict. Keywords had never been tested. LastName=downing with Keywords=zqxwvkj returns 0 where the same search without it returns 231,425, and with Keywords=pooley returns 12. KEYWORDS FILTERS. Added to the driver note, because a filter that only ranks is how a nil return becomes a lie.
yes
And under KING, the other surname the trees give her?
NOTHING THAT FITS — AND THE KEYWORD FIELD IS POISONED

“King” as a keyword returns 144 records for 1790–1806 and ALMOST EVERY ONE IS KING’S LYNN. A surname that is also half a place-name destroys the field. Run properly on SpouseLastName, DOWNING × KING for 1790–1806 RETURNS THREE RECORDS AND THEY ARE ONE NORFOLK EVENT INDEXED THREE TIMES — a MARY DOWNING at King’s Lynn and Norwich in 1790. Wrong person, wrong county, wrong direction. UNDER EITHER SURNAME THERE IS NO LONDON MARRIAGE FOR A JOHN DOWNING in the years this family needs.
no
Is there a better filter field than Keywords for a marriage?
YES — SpouseLastName, AND IT IS NOT IN THE DRIVER NOTES

The marriage transcripts carry SpouseFirstName and SpouseLastName as fieldIds, and SpouseLastName WORKS AS A FILTER: a nonsense value returns 0, “pooley” returns exactly the three indexed Downing–Pooley marriages. IT IS THE RIGHT TOOL FOR A MARRIAGE SEARCH and it is immune to the King’s Lynn problem. Added to the driver note in notes/for-the-estate.md, along with the finding that KEYWORDS FILTERS where KeywordsPlace only scores.
yes
